general_background.title: Making a soluble cadmium feed
general_background.summary: A carboxylic acid such as oleic acid can convert cadmium oxide into cadmium carboxylate in the flask. Changing this soluble feed and the free acid changes cadmium availability during nucleation and growth.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

reference.title: Formation of High-Quality CdTe, CdSe, and CdS Nanocrystals Using CdO as Precursor

general_background.title: A phosphine-free selenium feed has different chemistry
general_background.summary: When used as a phosphine-free feed in non-injection cadmium selenide synthesis, selenium dispersed or dissolved in octadecene has different conversion chemistry from phosphine-bound selenium. The choice of reaction medium changes the supply of growth species and can shift the balance between discrete clusters and continued growth.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

reference.title: Thermodynamic Equilibrium-Driven Formation of Single-Sized Nanocrystals: Reaction Media Tuning CdSe Magic-Sized versus Regular Quantum Dots

general_background.title: Octadecene is not always inert
general_background.summary: Octadecene provides a weakly coordinating medium for hot solution growth, leaving the ligands more freedom to control surface binding. It can also polymerize under growth conditions, leaving an alkene-derived residue that is difficult to separate from hydrophobic nanocrystals.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

reference.title: The Trouble with ODE: Polymerization during Nanocrystal Synthesis

general_background.title: Myristate binds indium and particle surfaces
general_background.summary: In colloidal indium phosphide synthesis, myristic acid can supply a carboxylate for soluble indium species and a stabilizing ligand for the growing solid. Carboxylate coordination can help determine which molecular intermediates persist during growth.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation
